subject: Trump ran on lowering prices. Now most Americans blame him for them.
posts:
Trump promised to lower prices, but a new poll shows 65% of Americans blame his policies for soaring costs.
Evidence: Campaign promises, AP/NORC poll data, public backlash
#Aletheia #USPol

Donald Trump ran heavily on lowering consumer prices and cost-of-living relief, claiming his economic plans would instantly ease household burdens.
Stated Judgement: (+0.5, 0.0) — Good Preference

Only 17% of Americans now approve of his economic handling. Rather than lower costs, voters overwhelmingly blame his policy choices for worsening inflation.
Resulting Judgement: (-0.8, -0.9) — Deception / Greater Evil

Verdict: FAIL — The Path of Deception. Campaign promises of easy economic relief collided with reality, shifting public blame entirely onto presidential policy.

Integrity: Severe Deception (Hypocrisy: 12.5, z: 3)

Sub-Audits Breakdown:
- Voter Cost-of-Living: FAIL (-0.80, -0.90) — 65% blame Trump policies.
- Presidential Messaging: FAIL (-0.75, -0.85) — Pretexts collide with inflation.
As cost pressures persist, public trust has plummeted to historic lows, matching pandemic-era dissatisfaction levels.

The Poison:
Pleasing rhetoric substitutes for structural economic reform, leaving citizens to bear the brunt of inflation.

The Breakdown & Plane Error:
Confusing political rhetoric (WHAT) with actual economic management (WHO). Campaign slogans masked structural policy failures.

Social Physics Analysis:
Trump ran a classic Smart Selfish maneuver: utilizing populist economic pretexts to capture power, while deflecting responsibility when inflation worsens.

The Trajectory: The Path of Deception.
When you map the gap between stated intentions and ground-level results, it plots a direct trajectory toward Greater Evil. Stated preferences collapse under empirical failure.

The Unavoidable Truth: Rhetorical promises cannot repeal global economic realities.

The Unavoidable Lie: Slogans alone can magically lower the cost of living.

Alethekanon:
Campaign claims of effortless economic revival collapse when everyday prices expose the emptiness of political pretexts.

Awwthekanon:
It hurts to watch families struggle with rising costs while politicians trade blame instead of offering real relief.

Brothekanon:
Turns out shouting you'll fix inflation doesn't actually lower grocery bills when the policies do the opposite.

Spirithekanon:
"Do not store up for yourselves treasures on earth" Matthew 6:19 FAIL
False promises of earthly prosperity leave empty hands.

Stated Claim / Post Context:
Trump ran on lowering prices. Now most Americans blame him for them.

An October poll also found that most blame Trump's policies for making affordability struggles worse.

Actual Article Body:
President Donald Trump sits during an event on health care affordability in the Oval Office on April 23, 2026.Mark Schiefelbein/AP

Only 17 percent of Americans approve of how President Donald Trump is handling the cost of living, according to a recent poll from the Associated Press and NORC Center for Public Affairs Research.

This is a record low for both of Trump’s presidential terms—notable as he spent much of his 2024 campaign criticizing Democrats on the issue. About 70 percent, including about half of Republicans, said the president’s cost-of-living policies have been “worse than expected.”

The Associated Press reported that Trump’s economic approval mirrors Biden’s 28 percent in June 2022 during the initial years of the Covid-19 pandemic. A few months later, 55 percent of Americans said that affordability struggles were outside his control. Actual Article Body:
Voters overwhelmingly want to keep the Supreme Court bench capped at nine justices, a new poll found, despite Democrats’ push to pack the court.

A new McLaughlin Associates poll found that voters overwhelmingly support keeping the Supreme Court at nine justices and back the “Keep Nine Amendment.”

The amendment sought to require that the Supreme Court be comprised of nine justices. Notably, nearly every single House Republican and one Democrat, Don Davis of North Carolina, supported the amendment during a Sept. 2 vote that came to 212-206. Fifteen members did not vote. The measure failed to get the two-thirds majority needed to pass it.

Federal judge blocks Trump administration fines of up to $1.8M for migrants

A federal judge blocked the Trump administration's migrant fines of up to $1.8 million, ruling DHS unlawfully imposed civil penalties for ignoring final deportation orders.

Podcast host Ben Domenech analyzes voter polling on border security and enforcement operations under the Trump administration.

A federal judge has blocked the Trump administration's attempts to fine migrants up to $1.8 million for failing to leave the country after receiving final deportation orders.

U.S. District Judge George O'Toole in Boston issued the ruling on Monday
